provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Graduation gratitude
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain the importance of thanksgiving in Christian life.
The pupils should be able to list ways to thank God for their primary school education.
Introduction:
We have completed our primary school journey and it is time to thank God. Last term we learned about God's faithfulness throughout the year.
Content:
Thanksgiving is showing gratitude to God for His blessings. Psalm 100:4 says Enter His gates with thanksgiving. We thank God for teachers who taught us like our mamas and papas. We thank God for friends who played with us during break time. We thank God for passing our exams and for our safety coming to school every day. Our thanksgiving service should have songs of praise like 'Count Your Blessings'. We should bring offerings to show our thankfulness to God.
Class activity:
Each pupil will write down three things they are thankful for from their primary school experience and share with the class.
Evaluation questions:
What is thanksgiving?
Why should we thank God for our primary school education?
Name two ways we can show gratitude to God during our thanksgiving service.
Summary:
We must always thank God for His goodness and faithfulness to us during our primary school years.

topics.title: David's leadership
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to describe how David became a leader.
The pupils should be able to explain what it means to lead with a heart for God.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about thanksgiving. Today we will learn about leadership from the life of David who was a great king of Israel.
Content:
David started as a shepherd boy looking after his father's sheep in the bush. He was chosen by God to be king because he had a heart for God. David led with courage when he fought Goliath with just a sling and stone. He led with humility when he spared King Saul's life. David led with worship by playing the harp and writing many Psalms. Good leaders like David put God first and care for those they lead like a good shepherd cares for his sheep.
Class activity:
Pupils will work in groups to act out how David showed good leadership when he was a shepherd and when he was king.
Evaluation questions:
How did David start his leadership journey?
What qualities made David a good leader?
How can we show good leadership like David in our school?
Summary:
True leadership comes from having a heart for God and serving others selflessly.

topics.title: Nehemiah rebuilds
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain Nehemiah's vision for Jerusalem.
The pupils should be able to identify the steps Nehemiah took to rebuild the walls.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about David's leadership. Today we will learn about Nehemiah who had a vision to rebuild broken walls.
Content:
Nehemiah saw that the walls of Jerusalem were broken down like when our school fence is damaged. He prayed to God about the problem. Nehemiah shared his vision with King Artaxerxes who helped him. He inspected the walls at night to see the damage. Nehemiah organized the people to work together with tools in hand. Some people built while others stood guard with spears. They rebuilt the walls in fifty-two days despite opposition. Like Nehemiah, we should have vision to fix what is broken in our community.
Class activity:
Pupils will draw a picture of the broken walls of Jerusalem and how Nehemiah and the people rebuilt them.
Evaluation questions:
What problem did Nehemiah see in Jerusalem?
What steps did Nehemiah take to rebuild the walls?
How can we apply Nehemiah's example in fixing problems in our school?
Summary:
With God's help and working together, we can rebuild what is broken in our community.

topics.title: Esther's courage
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to tell the story of Esther's courage.
The pupils should be able to explain how Esther stood for others in danger.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about Nehemiah rebuilding walls. Today we will learn about Esther who showed great courage to save her people.
Content:
Esther became a queen in a foreign land like a Nigerian girl becoming important in another country. Her cousin Mordecai told her she was born for such a time as this to help their people. The wicked Haman wanted to kill all Jews including Esther. Esther was afraid to go to the king without being called. She fasted and prayed for three days first. Then Esther put on her royal clothes and went to the king even though it was dangerous. She said if I perish, I perish but I must save my people. Esther's courage saved the Jewish people from destruction.
Class activity:
Pupils will role-play the scene where Esther goes to the king to ask for help to save her people.
Evaluation questions:
What was the danger Esther's people faced?
What gave Esther courage to go to the king?
How can we show courage like Esther to help others in need?
Summary:
God gives us courage to stand for others even when we are afraid.

topics.title: Daniel's discipline
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain Daniel's daily prayer discipline.
The pupils should be able to identify how Daniel showed integrity in difficult situations.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about Esther's courage. Today we will learn about Daniel who was known for his discipline and integrity.
Content:
Daniel prayed three times a day like we pray morning, afternoon and evening. Even when a law was made not to pray, Daniel continued to pray facing Jerusalem. Daniel showed integrity when he refused to eat the king's food that was against God's law. He asked for vegetables and water instead. Daniel continued to pray even when thrown into the lion's den. God protected Daniel because of his faithfulness. Like Daniel, we should have daily disciplines of prayer and always do what is right even when it is difficult.
Class activity:
Pupils will write down their daily prayer schedule and share one way they can show integrity like Daniel this week.
Evaluation questions:
What was Daniel's daily prayer habit?
How did Daniel show integrity when offered the king's food?
What happened to Daniel when he continued to pray despite the law?
Summary:
Daniel's discipline and integrity pleased God and protected him from danger.

topics.title: The great commission
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state the great commission given by Jesus.
The pupils should be able to explain how they can share their faith in their daily lives.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about Daniel's discipline. Today we will learn about Jesus' last command to His disciples before He went to heaven.
Content:
Jesus said go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, Son and Holy Spirit. This is called the great commission. We can share our faith by telling our friends about Jesus like sharing good news. We can share by helping others like when we share our textbooks with classmates who need help. We can share by living good lives so others see Jesus in us. Our school, market and homes are our mission fields where we can tell others about Jesus.
Class activity:
Pupils will prepare a short testimony about how Jesus has helped them and practice sharing it with a partner.
Evaluation questions:
What is the great commission?
Name three ways we can share our faith in our daily lives.
Where can we find our mission fields as primary six pupils?
Summary:
Jesus wants us to tell others about Him in all places and in all ways we can.

topics.title: Walking in the Spirit
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list the fruit of the Spirit.
The pupils should be able to explain how to develop Spirit-led habits.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about the great commission to share our faith. Today we will learn about how the Holy Spirit helps us live for God.
Content:
The Holy Spirit produces fruit in our lives like love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control. When we walk in the Spirit, we show these qualities to others. Spirit-led habits include praying every morning, reading our Bible like reading our textbook, and listening to the Holy Spirit's voice. When we are angry, the Spirit helps us to be patient. When we are sad, the Spirit gives us joy. The more we practice these habits, the more the Spirit's fruit grows in us.
Class activity:
Pupils will create a fruit of the Spirit chart and write down situations where they can show each fruit.
Evaluation questions:
Name three fruits of the Spirit.
How can we develop the habit of listening to the Holy Spirit?
What happens when we walk in the Spirit daily?
Summary:
The Holy Spirit helps us produce good fruit in our lives when we walk with Him daily.

topics.title: Eternal perspective
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain what it means to store treasures in heaven.
The pupils should be able to describe how to live with the end in mind.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about walking in the Spirit. Today we will learn about having an eternal perspective that focuses on heaven.
Content:
Jesus said store up for yourselves treasures in heaven where moths and rust cannot destroy. This means we should focus on things that have lasting value like helping others, sharing the gospel and growing in our relationship with God. Living with the end in mind means remembering that this life is temporary but heaven is forever. When we face difficulties, we remember that our reward in heaven is greater. When we make choices, we think about what God will say when we stand before Him. Like Joseph in the Bible, we should live in a way that honors God now for eternity.
Class activity:
Pupils will write down three things they can do this week that have eternal value.
Evaluation questions:
What does Jesus mean by storing treasures in heaven?
How does having an eternal perspective help us make good choices?
Name one way you can live with the end in mind at school.
Summary:
We should focus on eternal things rather than temporary pleasures as we prepare for heaven.

topics.title: Commissioning service
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain the importance of prayer for primary six pupils.
The pupils should be able to participate in blessings prayers for their future.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about having an eternal perspective. Today we will learn about our commissioning service as we prepare to leave primary school.
Introduction:
Our commissioning service is a special time when the church and school pray for us as we move to secondary school. This is like when our parents bless us before we go on a long journey.
Content:
During the commissioning service, our teachers and parents will pray for us. They will pray for wisdom in our studies as we face new subjects in secondary school. They will pray for protection as we travel to and from school. They will pray for good friends who will help us grow spiritually. They will pray for us to be bold witnesses for Jesus in our new schools. We should come with humble hearts and thanksgiving to receive these blessings.
Class activity:
Pupils will write down a prayer request for their secondary school journey and share it in small groups.
Evaluation questions:
What is a commissioning service?
What are some things people will pray for during our commissioning service?
How should we prepare our hearts for the commissioning service?
Summary:
The commissioning service is a special time of blessing and prayer as we transition to secondary school.

topics.title: Revision and thanksgiving
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recall what they learned this term.
The pupils should be able to participate in praise and thanksgiving to God.
Introduction:
This week we will revise all we learned this term and thank God for His faithfulness throughout the year.
Content:
We have learned about gratitude, leadership, rebuilding, courage, discipline, sharing our faith, walking in the Spirit, eternal perspective and commissioning. We should remember that God has been with us all through primary school. We have learned to trust God like David, to be courageous like Esther, to be disciplined like Daniel, and to share our faith like Jesus commanded. Our praise concert will have songs like 'We Give Thanks' and 'Blessed Assurance'. We should bring our offerings with joyful hearts to thank God for His goodness to us this year.
Class activity:
Pupils will work in groups to create a song or poem that summarizes what they learned this term and present it to the class.
Evaluation questions:
What was your favorite lesson this term and why?
Name three things God has done for you this year.
How can we show gratitude to God during our praise concert?
Summary:
We thank God for all He has taught us and done for us this year as we prepare to move forward in His plan.
